'''Jules Horowitz''' (3 October 1921{{snd}}3 August 1995) was a French physicist. The [[Jules Horowitz Reactor]] is named after him.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About - RJH - Jules Horowitz Reactor |url=https://jhrreactor.com/en/about/#why-call-it-the-jhr |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=jhrreactor.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Jules Horowitz was born to a Polish Jewish family in [[Rzeszów]], Poland. His parents, most likely in order to seek refuge for their children and themselves from the [[antisemitism]] in strongly catholic [[Poland]], emigrated to [[Weimar Republic|Weimar Germany]]. However, some years later they resumed their exodus westwards to escape the [[Nazism|National Socialist]] regime, ending up at [[Metz]]. They then moved once again to avoid living under the [[German military administration in occupied France during World War II|Nazi regime occupying France]], leaving Lorraine for the [[Zone libre|Zone libre]].

In 1941, Horowitz passed the entrance exam for [[École polytechnique|L'Ecole Polytechnique]]. The school had, since June 1940, abandoned its former location on the rue Descartes in Paris to move to Lyon and the Zone libre, and loses its military status. When the school returned to Paris in April 1943 after the invasion of the Zone Libre by the Germans in November 1942, Horowitz probably stayed in the south like his fellow students (denoted "bis" by the administration), having been naturalised at least 8 years earlier and being of Jewish faith.

A great contributor to [[nuclear physics]] through his work at the heart of the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|Commissariat à l'énergie atomique]] (CEA), he acted as director of the Department for Atomic Piles for the construction of the [[Zoé (reactor)|Zoé reactor]] (the first French atomic reactor). He applied his common sense to identify the deception in the [[Great Oil Sniffer Hoax]].

He was, in 1975, the creator and first director of the Institute of Fundamental Physics research at CEA, renamed Material Science Research, and today called [[:fr:Direction de la recherche fondamentale|La Direction de la recherche fondamentale]] (DRF). Instigator of the [[:fr: Laue-Langevin Institute|Laue-Langevin Institute]] i the early 1960s, he was also president of the [[board of directors]] at the [[European Synchrotron Radiation Facility]] during its creation (1988 to 1993).

He was presented {{clarify|date=September 2026}} as one of the major actors behind the [[:fr:programme nucléaire israélien|Israeli nuclear programme]]. He was furthermore the brother-in-law of the French physicist [[Claude Bloch]].{{authority control}}
